tree.heading: Definition of costs
tree.text: In this section, the term “costs”, when used with respect to review and decisionmaking pertaining to an application for which registration service fees are paid under this section, means—

children.text: costs to the extent that—

officers and employees provide direct support for the review and decisionmaking for covered pesticide applications, associated tolerances, and corresponding risk and benefits information and analyses;
persons and organizations under contract with the Administrator engage in the review of the applications, and corresponding risk and benefits information and assessments; and

advisory committees and other accredited persons or organizations, on the request of the Administrator, engage in the peer review of risk or benefits information associated with covered pesticide applications;

costs of management of information, and the acquisition, maintenance, and repair of computer and telecommunication resources (including software), used to support review of pesticide applications, associated tolerances, and corresponding risk and benefits information and analyses; and
costs of collecting registration service fees under subsections (b) and (c) and reporting, auditing, and accounting under this section.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Effective beginning on the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2003, the Administrator shall assess and collect covered pesticide registration service fees in accordance with this section.

children.heading: In general
children.text: An application for the registration of a pesticide covered by this subchapter that is received by the Administrator on or after the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2003 or for any other action covered by a table specified in paragraph (3)(B) shall be subject to a registration service fee under this section.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to clause (ii), an application for the registration of a pesticide that was submitted to the Administrator before the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2003 and is pending on that effective date shall be subject to a service fee under this section if the application is for the registration of a new active ingredient that is not listed in the Registration Division 2003 Work Plan of the Office of Pesticide Programs of the Environmental Protection Agency.

children.heading: Tolerance or exemption fees
children.text: The amount of any fee otherwise payable for an application described in clause (i) under this section shall be reduced by the amount of any fees paid to support the related petition for a pesticide tolerance or exemption under the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 301 et seq.).

children.heading: Documentation
children.text: An application subject to a registration service fee under this section shall be submitted with documentation certifying—
payment of the registration service fee; or
payment of at least 25 percent of the registration service fee and a request for a waiver from or reduction of the remaining amount of the registration service fee.

children.heading: Payment
children.text: The registration service fee required under this subsection shall be due upon submission of the application.

children.heading: Applications subject to additional fees
children.text: An application may be subject to additional fees if—
the applicant identified the incorrect registration service fee and decision review period;
after review of a waiver request, the Administrator denies the waiver request; or

on completion of, where appropriate, the initial screening of the contents of the application or the preliminary technical screening of the application, the Administrator determines that a different registration service fee and decision review period apply to the application.

children.heading: Effect of failure to pay fees
children.text: The Administrator shall reject any application submitted without the required registration service fee.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator shall retain 25 percent of the applicable registration service fee.

children.heading: Limitation
children.text: Any waiver, refund, credit or other reduction in the registration service fee shall not exceed 75 percent of the registration service fee.

children.heading: Collection of unpaid fees
children.text: In any case in which the Administrator does not receive payment of a registration service fee (or applicable portion of the registration service fee) by the date that is 30 days after the fee is due, the fee shall be treated as a claim of the United States Government subject to subchapter II of chapter 37 of title 31.

children.heading: Schedule of covered applications and other actions and their registration service fees
Data evaluation records
children.text: At the decision review time under a fee table specified in subparagraph (B) or as agreed upon under subsection (f)(5), for each covered application under a fee table specified in such subparagraph (B), the Administrator shall—
complete data evaluation records for studies submitted by the applicant in support of the application; and
release those data evaluation records to the applicant, using appropriate protections for confidential business information.

children.heading: In general
children.text: An applicant that submitted a registration application to the Administrator before the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2003, but that is not required to pay a registration service fee under paragraph (2)(B), may, on a voluntary basis, pay a registration service fee in accordance with paragraph (2)(B).

children.heading: Voluntary fee
children.text: The Administrator may not compel payment of a registration service fee for an application described in subparagraph (A).

children.heading: Documentation
children.text: An application for which a voluntary registration service fee is paid under this paragraph shall be submitted with documentation certifying—
payment of the registration service fee; or
a request for a waiver from or reduction of the registration service fee.

children.heading: Resubmission of covered applications
children.text: If a covered application is submitted by a person that paid the fee for the application under paragraph (2), is determined by the Administrator to be complete, and is not approved or is withdrawn (without a waiver or refund), the submission of the same covered application by the same person (or a licensee, assignee, or successor of the person) shall not be subject to a fee under paragraph (2).

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to the following sentence, effective for a covered application received during the period beginning on October 1, 2024, and ending on September 30, 2026, the Administrator may increase by 5 percent the registration service fee payable for the application under paragraph (3).1 No adjustment may be made under the preceding sentence until the date on which the Administrator begins to implement clauses (i) and (ii) of subsection (k)(2)(A).

children.heading: Additional adjustment
children.text: Subject to the following sentence, effective for a covered application received on or after October 1, 2026, the Administrator may increase by an additional 5 percent the registration service fee in effect as of September 30, 2026. No adjustment may be made under the preceding sentence until the date on which the Administrator begins to implement any recommendations for process improvements contained in the report under subsection (c)(4), as appropriate.

children.heading: Publication
children.text: The Administrator shall publish in the Federal Register the service fee schedules revised pursuant to this paragraph.

children.heading: In general
children.text: An applicant for a covered application may request the Administrator to waive or reduce the amount of a registration service fee payable under this section under the circumstances described in subparagraphs (D) through (G), except that no waiver or fee reduction shall be provided in connection with a request for a letter of certification (including a Gold Seal letter and a Certificate of Establishment).

children.heading: In general
children.text: A request for a waiver from or reduction of the registration service fee shall be accompanied by appropriate documentation demonstrating the basis for the waiver or reduction.

children.heading: Certification
children.text: The applicant shall provide to the Administrator a written certification, signed by a responsible officer, that the documentation submitted to support the waiver or reduction request is accurate.

children.heading: Inaccurate documentation
children.text: An application shall be subject to the applicable registration service fee payable under paragraph (3)(B) if, at any time, the Administrator determines that—
the documentation supporting the waiver or reduction request is not accurate; or
based on the documentation or any other information, the waiver or reduction should not have been granted or should not be granted.

children.heading: Determination to grant or deny request
children.text: As soon as practicable, but not later than 60 days, after the date on which the Administrator receives a request for a waiver or reduction of a registration service fee under this paragraph, the Administrator shall—
determine whether to grant or deny the request; and
notify the applicant of the determination.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator may exempt from, or waive a portion of, the registration service fee for an application for minor uses for a pesticide.

children.heading: Supporting documentation
children.text: An applicant requesting a waiver or exemption under this subparagraph shall provide supporting documentation that demonstrates, to the satisfaction of the Administrator, that anticipated revenues from the uses that are the subject of the application would be insufficient to justify imposition of the full application fee.

children.heading: IR–4 exemption
children.text: The Administrator shall exempt an application from the registration service fee if the Administrator determines that—

the application is solely associated with a tolerance petition submitted in connection with the Inter-Regional Project Number 4 (IR–4) as described in section 2 of Public Law 89–106 (7 U.S.C. 450i(e)); 1 and
the exemption is in the public interest.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator shall waive 50 percent of the registration service fees payable by an entity for a covered application under this section if the entity is a small business (as defined in section 136a–1(i)(1)(E)(ii) of this title) at the time of application.

children.heading: Waiver of fees
children.text: The Administrator shall waive 75 percent of the registration service fees payable by an entity under this section if the entity—
is a small business (as defined in section 136a–1(i)(1)(E)(ii) of this title) at the time of application; and
has average annual global gross revenues described in section 136a–1(i)(1)(E)(ii)(I)(bb) of this title that does not exceed $10,000,000, at the time of application.

children.heading: Formation for waiver
children.text: The Administrator shall not grant a waiver under this subparagraph if the Administrator determines that the entity submitting the application has been formed or manipulated primarily for the purpose of qualifying for the waiver.

children.heading: Documentation
children.text: An entity requesting a waiver under this subparagraph shall provide to the Administrator—
documentation demonstrating that the entity is a small business (as defined in section 136a–1(i)(1)(E)(ii) of this title) at the time of application; and

if the entity is requesting a waiver of 75 percent of the applicable registration service fees payable under this section, documentation demonstrating that the entity has an average annual global gross revenue described in section 136a–1(i)(1)(E)(ii)(I)(bb) of this title that does not exceed $10,000,000, at the time of application.

children.heading: Federal and State agency exemptions
children.text: An agency of the Federal Government or a State government shall be exempt from covered registration service fees under this section.

children.heading: Early withdrawals
children.text: If, during the first 60 days after the beginning of the applicable decision time review period under subsection (f)(3), a covered application is withdrawn by the applicant, the Administrator shall refund all but 25 percent.2 of the total registration service fee payable under paragraph (3)(B) for the application.

children.heading: Withdrawals after the first 60 days of decision review time period
In general
children.text: If a covered application is withdrawn after the first 60 days of the applicable decision time review period, the Administrator shall determine what portion, if any, of the total registration service fee payable under paragraph (3)(B) for the application may be refunded based on the proportion of the work completed at the time of withdrawal.

children.heading: Timing
children.text: The Administrator shall—
make the determination described in clause (i) not later than 90 days after the date the application is withdrawn; and
provide any refund as soon as practicable after the determination.

children.heading: In general
children.text: In the case of a covered application that has been filed with the Administrator and has not been withdrawn by the applicant, but for which the Administrator has not yet made a final determination, the Administrator may refund a portion of a covered registration service fee if the Administrator determines that the refund is justified.

children.heading: Basis
children.text: The Administrator may provide a refund for an application under this subparagraph—
on the basis that, in reviewing the application, the Administrator has considered data submitted in support of another covered application;
on the basis that the Administrator completed portions of the review of the application before the effective date of this section; or
on the basis that the Administrator rejected the application under subsection (f)(4)(B).

children.heading: Credited fees
children.text: In determining whether to grant a refund under this paragraph, the Administrator shall take into account any portion of the registration service fees credited under paragraph (2) or (4).

children.heading: Establishment
children.text: There is established in the Treasury of the United States a Pesticide Registration Fund to be used in carrying out this section (referred to in this section as the “Fund”), consisting of—
such amounts as are deposited in the Fund under paragraph (2);
any interest earned on investment of amounts in the Fund under paragraph (5); and
any proceeds from the sale or redemption of investments held in the Fund.

children.heading: Deposits in Fund
children.text: Subject to paragraph (4), the Administrator shall deposit fees collected under this section in the Fund.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Subject to subparagraphs (B) and (C) and paragraph (4), the Administrator may make expenditures from the Fund—
to cover the costs associated with the review and decisionmaking pertaining to all applications for which registration service fees have been paid under this section; and
to otherwise carry out this section.

children.heading: Endangered species review of outdoor use of pesticide products
In general
children.text: The Administrator shall use the amounts made available in the Fund to develop, receive comments with respect to, and finalize, guidance to registrants regarding analysis necessary to support the review of outdoor uses of pesticide products under the Endangered Species Act of 1973 (16 U.S.C. 1531 et seq.).

children.heading: Deadlines for guidance
children.text: The Administrator shall issue final guidance required by clause (i) in accordance with the following:
With respect to new active ingredients or any registration review decision proposed for 1 or more outdoor uses, not later than 9 months after December 29, 2022.
With respect to new outdoor uses of a registered pesticide, not later than 1 year after December 29, 2022.
With respect to antimicrobial pesticide products, not later than 3 years after December 29, 2022.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator shall use the amounts made available in the Fund to carry out the activities described in clauses (ii) and (iii).

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator shall procure a competitive contract with a qualified, independent contractor with expertise in assessing public sector workforce data analysis and reporting to conduct an assessment of current methodologies and data or metrics available to represent the workforce implementing the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2022 and the amendments made by that Act, including an assessment of filled and vacant positions and full-time equivalent employees relating to that implementation.

children.heading: Report
children.text: Not later than 2 years after December 29, 2022—
the contractor selected under subclause (I) shall submit to the Administrator a report describing—
the findings from the assessment under that subclause; and
recommendations for improved methodologies to represent full-time equivalent resources described in that subclause; and
the Administrator shall publish the report submitted under item (aa) on the website of the Environmental Protection Agency.

children.heading: Contracts
children.text: Within 1 year of December 29, 2022, to the extent practicable, the Administrator shall issue a competitive contract to a private, independent consulting firm—
to conduct the assessment described in subclause (II); and

to submit to the Administrator a report describing the findings of the assessment and the processes and performance of the Environmental Protection Agency relating to the implementation of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2022 and the amendments made by that Act.

children.heading: Eligibility
children.text: The firm described in item (aa) shall be capable of performing the technical analysis, management assessment, and program evaluation tasks required to address the scope of the assessment under subclause (II).

children.heading: In general
children.text: The Administrator, applicants, and registrants shall participate in a targeted assessment of the process for the review of applications submitted under this subchapter.

children.heading: Consultation
children.text: The firm selected under subclause (I) shall consult with the Administrator and applicants at the start of the assessment under item (aa) and prior to submission of the report under subclause (I)(aa)(BB).

children.heading: Requirements
children.text: The assessment under item (aa) shall evaluate and make recommendations regarding—
the initial content screen;
the preliminary technical screen;
performance, processes, and progress toward reducing renegotiation rates and the average length of renegotiations;
performance, processes, and progress toward eliminating the backlog of registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3);

performance, processes, and progress toward ensuring that all registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3) are completed by the applicable deadlines described in the notice of the Administrator entitled “Pesticide Registration Notice (PR) 98–10: Notifications, Non-Notifications and Minor Formulation Amendments” and dated October 22, 1998 (and any successor amendments to that notice) and described in subsections (c)(3)(B) and (h) of section 136a of this title;
compliance with the provisions of this subchapter relating to renegotiations and registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3);
information technology systems;
recommended improvements to employee training;
performance, progress, and processes in completing registration review; and
other appropriate issues, such as submissions by inert suppliers and fast-track amendments under subsections (c)(3)(B) and (h) of section 136a of this title.

children.heading: Report to Congress
children.text: Not later than 1 year after the receipt of an assessment required under this section, the Administrator shall submit to the Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry of the Senate and the Committee on Agriculture of the House of Representatives—
a copy of each such assessment; and
the Administrator’s evaluation of the findings and recommendations contained in each such assessment.

children.heading: Recommendations
children.text: The Administrator shall include with the report submitted under subclause (III) a classification of each recommendation described in the report as—
can be implemented through administrative action of the Administrator; or
requires a statutory change.

children.heading: Collections and appropriations Acts
children.text: The fees authorized by this section and amounts deposited in the Fund—
shall be collected and made available for obligation only to the extent provided in advance in appropriations Acts;
shall be available during periods in which Environmental Protection Agency employees are on shutdown or emergency furlough as a result of a lapse in appropriations; and
shall be available without fiscal year limitation.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Amounts in the Fund not currently needed to carry out this section shall be—
maintained readily available or on deposit;
invested in obligations of the United States or guaranteed by the United States; or
invested in obligations, participations, or other instruments that are lawful investments for fiduciary, trust, or public funds.

children.heading: Use of investment income
children.text: After consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury, the Administrator may use income from investments described in clauses (ii) and (iii) of subparagraph (A) to carry out this section.

children.heading: Definition of covered functions
children.text: In this subsection, the term “covered functions” means functions of the Office of Pesticide Programs of the Environmental Protection Agency, as identified in key programs and projects of the final operating plan for the Environmental Protection Agency submitted as part of the budget process for fiscal year 2002, regardless of any subsequent transfer of 1 or more of the functions to another office or agency or the subsequent transfer of a new function to the Office of Pesticide Programs.

children.heading: Minimum amount of appropriations
children.text: Registration service fees may not be assessed for a fiscal year under this section unless the amount of appropriations for salaries, contracts, and expenses for the functions of the Office of Pesticide Programs of the Environmental Protection Agency for the fiscal year (excluding the amount of any fees appropriated for the fiscal year) are equal to or greater than $166,000,000.

children.heading: Use of fees
children.text: Registration service fees authorized by this section shall be available, in the aggregate, only to defray increases in the costs associated with the review and decisionmaking for the review of pesticide registration applications and associated tolerances (including increases in the number of full-time equivalent positions in the Environmental Protection Agency engaged in those activities) over the costs for fiscal year 2002, excluding costs paid from fees appropriated for the fiscal year.

children.heading: Subsequent authority
children.text: If the Administrator does not assess registration service fees under subsection (b) during any portion of a fiscal year as the result of paragraph (2) and is subsequently permitted to assess the fees under subsection (b) during the fiscal year, the Administrator shall assess and collect the fees, without any modification in rate, at any time during the fiscal year, notwithstanding any provisions of subsection (b) relating to the date fees are to be paid.

tree.heading: Reforms to reduce decision time review periods and prevent double payment of registration fees

children.heading: Reduction of decision time review periods
children.text: To the maximum extent practicable consistent with the degrees of risk presented by pesticides and the type of review appropriate to evaluate risks, the Administrator shall identify and evaluate reforms to the pesticide registration process under this subchapter with the goal of reducing decision review periods in effect on the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Extension Act of 2018 for pesticide registration actions for covered pesticide registration applications (including reduced risk applications). Such reforms shall include identifying opportunities for streamlining review processes for applications for a new active ingredient or a new use and providing prompt feedback to applicants during such review process.

children.heading: Prevention of double payment of registration service fees
children.text: The Administrator shall develop and implement a process to determine the appropriate fee category or categories for an application that qualifies for more than one fee category in order to assist applicants and prevent unnecessary payment of fees for multiple categories for a single application.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Not later than 30 days after the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2022, the Administrator shall make publicly available a schedule of decision review periods for covered pesticide registration actions or for any other action covered by a table specified in subsection (b)(3)(B) and corresponding registration service fees under this subchapter.

children.heading: Report
children.text: The schedule shall be the same as the applicable schedule provided under subsection (b)(3)(B).

children.heading: Applications subject to decision time review periods
children.text: The decision time review periods specified in paragraph (1) shall apply to—
covered pesticide registration applications subject to registration service fees under subsection (b)(2);
covered pesticide registration applications for which an applicant has voluntarily paid registration service fees under subsection (b)(4); and
applications for any other action covered by a table specified in subsection (b)(3)(B).

children.heading: Start of decision time review period
In general
children.text: Except as provided in subparagraphs (C), (D), and (E), in the case of a covered application accompanied by the registration service fee required under this section, the decision time review period begins 21 days after the date on which the Administrator receives the covered application and fee.

children.heading: Initial content and preliminary technical screenings
Initial content
children.text: Not later than 21 days after receiving an application and the required registration service fee, the Administrator shall conduct an initial screening of the contents of the application in accordance with clause (iii).

children.heading: Preliminary technical screening
children.text: After conducting the initial content screening described in subclause (I) and in accordance with clause (iv), the Administrator shall conduct a preliminary technical screening—
not later than 45 days after the date on which the decision time review period begins (for applications with decision time review periods of not more than 180 days); and
not later than 90 days after the date on which the decision time review period begins (for applications with decision time review periods greater than 180 days).

children.heading: Final fee category
children.text: The fee category of a covered application or other actions may not be changed, without providing the information to the applicant, after completion of the preliminary technical screening described in clause (iv).

children.heading: In general
children.text: If the Administrator determines at any time before the Administrator completes the preliminary technical screening under clause (i)(II) that the application failed the initial content or preliminary technical screening and the applicant does not correct the failure before the date that is 10 business days after the applicant receives a notification of the failure, the Administrator shall reject the application.

children.heading: Written notification
children.text: The Administrator shall make every effort to provide a written notification of a rejection under subclause (I) during the 10-day period that begins on the date the Administrator completes the preliminary technical screening.

children.heading: Requirements of initial content screening
children.text: In conducting an initial content screening of an application, the Administrator shall automate the process, to the maximum extent practicable, and determine whether—
the applicable registration service fee has been paid; or

at least 25 percent of the applicable registration service fee has been paid and the application contains a waiver or refund request for the outstanding amount and documentation establishing the basis for the waiver request; and
the application appears to contain all the necessary forms, data, and draft labeling, formatted in accordance with guidance published by the Administrator.

children.heading: Requirements of preliminary technical screening
children.text: In conducting a preliminary technical screening of an application, the Administrator shall—
determine if the application and the data and information submitted with the application are accurate and complete;

determine if the application, data, and information are consistent with the proposed labeling and any proposal for a tolerance or exemption from the requirement for a tolerance under section 408 of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (21 U.S.C. 346a), and are such that, subject to full review under the standards of this subchapter, could result in the granting of the application;
determine, if applicable, whether an application qualifies for a reduced risk determination under subsection (c)(10) or (h) of section 136a of this title;
grant or deny any data waiver requests submitted by the applicant with the application;
verify and validate the accuracy of the fee category selected by the applicant; and
notify the applicant, in writing, if a new or different fee category is required and calculate the new decision review time based on the original submission date.

children.heading: Applications with waiver or reduction requests
In general
children.text: In the case of an application submitted with a request for a waiver or reduction of registration service fees under subsection (b)(7), the decision time review period shall be determined in accordance with this subparagraph.

children.heading: Request granted with no additional fees required
children.text: If the Administrator grants the waiver or reduction request and no additional fee is required, the decision time review period begins on the earlier of—
the date on which the Administrator grants the request; or
the date that is 60 days after the date of receipt of the application.

children.heading: Request granted with additional fees required
children.text: If the Administrator grants the waiver or reduction request, in whole or in part, but an additional registration service fee is required, the decision time review period begins on the date on which the Administrator receives certification of payment of the applicable registration service fee.

children.heading: Request denied
children.text: If the Administrator denies the waiver or reduction request, the decision time review period begins on the date on which the Administrator receives certification of payment of the applicable registration service fee.

children.heading: In general
children.text: The start of the decision time review period for applications described in clause (ii) shall be the date on which the Administrator receives certification of payment of the applicable registration service fee.

children.heading: Applications
children.text: Clause (i) applies to—
covered pesticide registration applications for which voluntary fees have been paid under subsection (b)(4); and

covered pesticide registration applications received on or after the effective date of the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2003 but submitted without the applicable registration service fee required under this section due to the inability of the Administrator to assess fees under subsection (d)(1).

children.heading: Fee
children.text: If an application for a reduced risk new active ingredient or a reduced risk new use is determined not to qualify as reduced risk, the applicant shall pay the difference in fee for the corresponding non-reduced risk application.

children.heading: Decision review time period
children.text: After receipt by the Administrator of the original covered reduced risk application and fee, the decision time review period for the corresponding non-reduced risk application shall begin within the time periods described in subparagraph (A), based on the submission date of the original covered reduced risk application.

children.heading: Extension of decision time review period
Notification
children.text: If the Administrator cannot meet a decision time review period under this subsection, the Administrator shall notify the applicant, in writing, of—
the reasons why additional time is needed; and
the number of days needed that would allow the Administrator to make a regulatory decision.

children.heading: Extension by negotiation or mutual agreement
children.text: The Administrator, acting solely through the Director of the Office of Pesticide Programs, and the applicant may mutually agree, in writing, to extend a decision time review period under this subsection if—

there is new or additional data or information from the applicant that is necessary for the Administrator to make a decision on the application that cannot be made available within the original decision time review period; or
a public comment period associated with the application generates significant comments that cannot be addressed within the original decision time review period.

children.heading: Priority
children.text: Once a decision time review period for a covered action described in subsection (b)(3)(B) is missed or extended, the Administrator shall make any action on the application a priority.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Any applicant adversely affected by the failure of the Administrator to make a determination on the application of the applicant for registration of a new active ingredient or new use for which a registration service fee is paid under this section may obtain judicial review of the failure solely under this section.

children.heading: In general
children.text: In an action brought under this subsection, the only issue on review is whether the Administrator failed to make a determination on the application specified in paragraph (1) by the end of the applicable decision time review period required under subsection (f) for the application.

children.heading: Other actions
children.text: No other action authorized or required under this section shall be judicially reviewable by a Federal or State court.

children.heading: In general
children.text: A person may not obtain judicial review of the failure of the Administrator to make a determination on the application specified in paragraph (1) before the expiration of the 2-year period that begins on the date on which the decision time review period for the application ends.

children.heading: Meeting with Administrator
children.text: To be eligible to seek judicial review under this subsection, a person seeking the review shall first request in writing, at least 120 days before filing the complaint for judicial review, a decision review meeting with the Administrator.

children.heading: Remedies
children.text: The Administrator may not be required or permitted to refund any portion of a registration service fee paid in response to a complaint that the Administrator has failed to make a determination on the covered pesticide registration application specified in paragraph (1) by the end of the applicable decision review period.
provide an annual accounting of the registration service fees paid to the Administrator and disbursed from the Fund, by providing financial statements in accordance with—
the Chief Financial Officers Act of 1990 (Public Law 101–576; 104 Stat. 2838) and amendments made by that Act; and
the Government Management Reform Act of 1994 (Public Law 103–356; 108 Stat. 3410) and amendments made by that Act;
provide an accounting describing expenditures from the Fund authorized under subsection (c); and
provide an annual accounting describing collections and expenditures authorized under subsection (d).

children.heading: Financial statements of agencies
children.text: For the purpose of section 3515(c) of title 31, the Fund shall be considered a component of an executive agency.

children.heading: Components
children.text: The annual audit required under sections 3515(b) and 3521 of that title of the financial statements of activities under this section shall include an analysis of—
the fees collected under subsection (b) and disbursed;
compliance with subsection (f);
the amount appropriated to meet the requirements of subsection (d)(1); and
the reasonableness of the allocation of the overhead allocation of costs associated with the review and decisionmaking pertaining to applications under this section.

children.heading: Inspector General
children.text: The Inspector General of the Environmental Protection Agency shall—
conduct the annual audit required under this subsection; and
report the findings and recommendations of the audit to the Administrator and to the appropriate committees of Congress.

tree.heading: Personnel levels
tree.text: All full-time equivalent positions supported by fees authorized and collected under this section shall not be counted against the agency-wide personnel level goals of the Environmental Protection Agency.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Not later than 120 days after the last day of each of fiscal years 2023 through 2027, the Administrator shall publish an annual report describing—
actions taken under this section;
registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3)(B);
the initial content and preliminary technical screenings required in subsection (f)(4)(B); and
staffing relating to implementing the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2022 and the amendments made by that Act.

children.heading: Contents
children.text: Each report published under subparagraph (A) shall include a summary of the following information:

children.heading: Actions under this section
children.text: To the extent practicable, data for each action taken under this section that is completed during the fiscal year covered by the report or pending at the conclusion of that fiscal year, organized by registering division, including—
the Action Code;
the application receipt date;
the electronic portal tracking number assigned to the application at the time of submission to the electronic submission portal or the Environmental Protection Agency tracking number;
the original decision due date based on the Action Code;
the dates of any renegotiations and the renegotiated due dates, if applicable;
the reasons for each renegotiation, if applicable;
if the submission had to be recoded, reassigned codes, if applicable;
the date that the submission was recoded, if applicable;
the decision completion date, if the action has been completed;
the status of the action, which may be—
failed initial content screen;
failed preliminary technical screen;
approved;
withdrawn;
denied;
do not grant; or
pending;
the reason for any denial or do not grant decision, if applicable;

a review of the progress made in carrying out each requirement of subsections (e) and (f), including, to the extent determined appropriate by the Administrator and consistent with the authorities of the Administrator and limitations on delegation of functions by the Administrator, recommendations for the allowance and use of summaries of acute toxicity studies;
a review of the progress in carrying out section 136a(g) of this title, including—
3 the number of pesticides or pesticide cases reviewed and the number of registration review decisions completed, including—
the number of cases cancelled;
the number of cases requiring risk mitigation measures;
the number of cases removing risk mitigation measures;
the number of cases with no risk mitigation needed; and
the number of cases in which risk mitigation has been fully implemented;
a review of the progress made toward implementing enhancements to—
the electronic tracking of conditional registrations; and
the endangered species database;

a review of the progress made in updating the Pesticide Incident Data System, including progress toward making the information contained in the System available to the public (as the Administrator determines is appropriate);
an assessment of the public availability of summary pesticide usage data;

the number of the active ingredients approved, new uses, and pesticide end use products granted in connection with the Design for the Environment program (or any successor program) of the Environmental Protection Agency;
with respect to funds in the Reregistration and Expedited Processing Fund described under section 136a–1(k) of this title, a review that includes—
a description of the amount and use of such funds—
to carry out activities relating to worker protection under subparagraphs (G) and (H) of section 136a–1(i)(1) of this title;
to award partnership grants under subparagraph (I) of such section; and
to carry out the pesticide safety education program under subparagraph (J) of such section;
an evaluation of the appropriateness and effectiveness of the activities, grants, and program under subparagraphs (G), (H), (I), and (J) of such section;
a description of how stakeholders are engaged in the decision to fund such activities, grants, and program in accordance with the stakeholder input provided under such subparagraphs; and

with respect to activities relating to worker protection carried out under subparagraphs (G) and (H) of section 136a–1(i)(1) of this title, a summary of the analyses from stakeholders, including from worker community-based organizations, on the appropriateness and effectiveness of such activities.
beginning two years after enactment, report on the progress of meeting the deadlines listed in paragraph (5) of section 136a(f) of this title; and
a review of progress made in implementing the pesticide surveillance program referred to in paragraph (8) of section 136a–1(k) of this title.

children.heading: Registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3)(B)
children.text: Each registrant submission not covered by subsection (b)(3)(B), that is completed during the fiscal year covered by the report or pending at the conclusion of that fiscal year, organized by registering division, including—
the submission date;
the electronic portal tracking number assigned to the application at the time of the submission of the application to the electronic submission portal;
the type of regulatory action, as defined by statute or guidance document, and the specific label action;
the status of the action;
the due date;
the reason for the outcome; and
the completion date, if applicable.

children.heading: Screening process
children.text: Data for the initial content screens and preliminary technical screens that are completed during the fiscal year covered by the report or pending at the conclusion of that fiscal year, organized by registering division, including—
the number of applications successfully passing each type of screen;
the number of applications that failed the screening process for each type of screen;
the number of notifications issued by the Administrator under subsection (f)(4)(B)(ii)(II);
the number of notifications issued by the Administrator under subsection (f)(4)(B)(ii)(I) and the number of applications resulting in a rejection; and
the number of notifications issued under section 152.105 of title 40, Code of Federal Regulations (or successor regulations), and to the extent practicable, the reasons for that issuance.

children.heading: Staffing
children.text: Data on the staffing relating to work covered under the Pesticide Registration Improvement Act of 2022 and the amendments made by that Act, organized by registering division, including—
the number of new hires and personnel departures;
the number of full-time equivalents at the end of each fiscal year;
the number of full-time equivalents working on registration review activities; and
the number of full-time equivalents working on registrant submissions not covered by subsection (b)(3)(B).

children.heading: Publication
children.text: The Administrator shall publish each report under subparagraph (A)—
on the website of the Environmental Protection Agency; and
by such other methods as the Administrator determines to be the most effective for efficiently disseminating the report.

children.heading: System
children.text: Not later than 1 year after December 29, 2022, the Administrator shall establish an information technology system that—
includes all registering divisions in the Office of Pesticide Programs;
provides a real-time, accurate, tracking system for all regulatory submissions to the Office of Pesticide Programs;
provides a 4 real-time, accessible information 4 that provides each applicant confidential, online access to the status and progress of the regulatory submissions of the applicant; and
updates the electronic submission portal—
to ensure that label reviews are limited to current label changes, to the maximum extent practicable;
to automate, to the extent practicable, minor, low risk regulatory actions; and
to allow self-certification of certain regulatory actions, as determined by the Administrator.

children.heading: Access to registration data and decisions
children.text: The Administrator shall implement efforts to expand existing, and develop new, information technology tools and databases to improve access by Environmental Protection Agency employees to data used to fulfill registrations, and public access to information about regulatory decisionmaking tools, including opportunities for—
analysis of the impact of submitted studies on Environmental Protection Agency assessments and decisions;
facilitation of read-across or computational model development to help fill information gaps;
tracking and reporting submission and decision metrics relating to the use and acceptance of test methods; and
drafting and publication of policies communicating Environmental Protection Agency acceptance of novel technologies or approaches.

tree.heading: Savings clause
tree.text: Nothing in this section affects any other duties, obligations, or authorities established by any other section of this subchapter, including the right to judicial review of duties, obligations, or authorities established by any other section of this subchapter.

children.heading: In general
children.text: Except as provided in paragraph (2), the authority provided by this section terminates on September 30, 2027.

children.heading: Fiscal year 2028
children.text: During fiscal year 2028, the requirement to pay and collect registration service fees applies, except that the level of registration service fees payable under this section shall be reduced 40 percent below the level in effect on September 30, 2027.

children.heading: Fiscal year 2029
children.text: During fiscal year 2029, the requirement to pay and collect registration service fees applies, except that the level of registration service fees payable under this section shall be reduced 70 percent below the level in effect on September 30, 2027.

children.heading: September 30, 2029
children.text: Effective September 30, 2029, the requirement to pay and collect registration service fees terminates.

children.heading: Pending applications
children.text: In the case of an application received under this section before September 30, 2027, the application shall be reviewed in accordance with subsection (f).

children.heading: New applications
children.text: In the case of an application received under this section on or after September 30, 2027, subsection (f) shall not apply to the application.
